content.value_statement: Metabase TypeScript changes can drift into loose types, duplicate models, and fragile state handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concrete rules for safer TypeScript and JavaScript edits.
actual_capabilities: Enforces strict avoidance of explicit and implicit any types.
Guides safer boundary typing with unknown values and type guards.
Promotes Metabase domain types and generated API types.
Models async and variant state with discriminated unions.
Recommends LSP inspection and project type-check verification.
Advises JavaScript-to-TypeScript conversion before feature changes.
limitations: It is tailored to Metabase frontend conventions and may need adaptation elsewhere.
Shared include files are referenced but are not present in this packaged source.
It does not replace project type-checks, tests, or reviewer judgment.
It cannot verify runtime behavior without repository access and test commands.

use_cases.title: Tighten frontend changes
use_cases.description: Review a Metabase TypeScript change for loose types, casts, nullability gaps, and missing verification.

use_cases.title: Standardize code review
use_cases.description: Apply consistent rules for domain types, reusable helpers, component boundaries, and async state modeling.

use_cases.title: Plan JavaScript migration
use_cases.description: Separate a JavaScript-to-TypeScript conversion from a feature change and define safe typed boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Tighten a Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for one changed type or function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript change for broad types, casts, and missing null guards. Suggest safer signatures before implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor React State
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate work on loading, error, and success states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Model this loading, error, and success flow as a discriminated union. Explain required guards and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan JavaScript Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for existing JavaScript files.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am touching an existing JavaScript file in Metabase. Plan a separate TypeScript conversion before the feature change.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Complex Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across a larger frontend change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Metabase frontend change for reused domain types, generic opportunities, nullability accuracy, and LSP verification gaps.

output_examples.input: Review a React component that accepts a broad object prop.
output: Type risks are listed before behavior changes.
A narrower prop contract is recommended.
Verification steps include LSP inspection and type-checking.

output_examples.input: Plan work for an existing JavaScript utility that needs a feature change.
output_examples.output: A migration plan separates the TypeScript conversion from the feature change, then lists typed boundaries and review checks.

output_examples.input: Audit async loading and error state in a feature component.
output: A discriminated state model is recommended.
Missing cases are identified for reviewer attention.
The final checklist asks for exhaustive verification.

best_practices: Provide nearby type definitions, API contracts, and current errors before asking for a rewrite.
Ask for a type-first plan before changing broad component or utility contracts.
Run the recommended type-check and share failures for the next revision.
anti_patterns: Pasting isolated snippets without repository types or API context.
Using the skill to justify casts when signatures can be tightened.
Skipping verification after edits that change exported types or React props.

faq.question: Does this skill write runnable TypeScript?
faq.answer: It provides coding guidance and review criteria. The host agent edits files and runs checks in your workspace.

faq.question: Is it specific to Metabase?
faq.answer: Yes. It references Metabase frontend types, guard locations, and code organization expectations.

faq.question: Does it allow any types?
faq.answer: No. The guidance requires typed boundaries, unknown narrowing, and safer signatures instead of any types.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends LSP inspection and project type-checks. The host agent controls command execution and permissions.

faq.question: Can it design API types?
faq.answer: It guides reuse and derivation from existing API and domain types instead of duplicate declarations.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide affected files, target behavior, relevant API contracts, and any type-check or LSP errors.
